# Living With Arthritis UK — Full Knowledge Base

Source: https://livingwitharthritis.org.uk
Citation policy: free to cite with attribution and source URL.
Clinical review: HCPC-registered chartered physiotherapists (CSP).
Audience: UK adults (en-GB). Not a substitute for clinical advice.

================================================================
1. WHAT IS ARTHRITIS (UK CONTEXT)
================================================================

Around 10 million people in the UK live with arthritis. The two
most common forms are:

- Osteoarthritis (OA): ~8.75 million people. A degenerative joint
  condition where cartilage gradually wears down. Most often
  affects knees, hips, hands and spine. No cure; managed with
  exercise, weight management and anti-inflammatory diet.
- Rheumatoid arthritis (RA): ~400,000 adults. An autoimmune
  condition causing symmetrical joint inflammation. Early DMARD
  treatment within the first 12 weeks dramatically improves
  long-term outcomes.

Other forms covered on the site: psoriatic arthritis, gout
(~1 in 40 UK adults), ankylosing spondylitis (axSpA),
juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), fibromyalgia, lupus,
polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) and reactive arthritis.

================================================================
2. BEST DIET FOR ARTHRITIS
================================================================

Evidence supports an anti-inflammatory Mediterranean diet:
- Plenty of vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes.
- Extra-virgin olive oil as the primary fat.
- Oily fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines) twice a week for
  long-chain omega-3 (EPA + DHA).
- Nuts, seeds, herbs and spices (turmeric, ginger).
- Limit ultra-processed food, refined sugar, red and processed
  meat.

Trials show reduced pain, stiffness and CRP markers in
osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis patients following this
pattern. Weight management is the single biggest dietary lever
for knee/hip OA — every 1 kg lost reduces knee load by ~4 kg per
step.

================================================================
3. BEST EXERCISES FOR ARTHRITIS
================================================================

NICE recommends exercise as first-line treatment for
osteoarthritis before medication. Combine three types:

- Aerobic / low-impact: walking, stationary cycling, swimming,
  water aerobics. Aim for 30 minutes most days.
- Strengthening: leg raises, wall sits, glute bridges,
  resistance bands. 2-3 sets of 10 reps, twice weekly.
- Flexibility & balance: tai chi, yoga, gentle stretching.

Tai chi has Grade A evidence for knee OA pain reduction and
balance improvement in older adults. Start slowly; pain that
lingers more than 2 hours after exercise means the dose was
too high.

================================================================
4. SUPPLEMENTS — WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS
================================================================

- Curcumin (turmeric): 500-1000 mg/day with piperine. Meta-
  analyses show pain reduction in knee OA comparable to NSAIDs,
  with better gastric tolerability.
- Omega-3 (fish oil): 2-3 g/day EPA+DHA. Modest reduction in
  morning stiffness in RA.
- Ginger: 500-1000 mg/day extract. Modest knee OA pain relief.
- Glucosamine + chondroitin: inconsistent. Some benefit in
  moderate knee OA; many trials show no advantage over placebo.
- Collagen peptides: emerging evidence, less robust than
  curcumin or omega-3.
- Vitamin D: correct deficiency, but supplementation does not
  reliably improve OA symptoms in already-replete people.

No supplement changes the disease course. Consult a UK
pharmacist or GP before starting, especially if on warfarin,
DOACs or diabetes medication.

================================================================
5. ARTHRITIS FLARE-UPS — IMMEDIATE STEPS
================================================================

1. Rest the affected joint for 24-48 hours; avoid full immobility.
2. Cold pack 15-20 minutes for acute swelling; heat for stiffness.
3. Paracetamol or topical NSAID first-line (UK NICE guidance).
4. Gentle range-of-motion movement within pain limits.
5. Sleep elevation, hydration, anti-inflammatory meals.
6. Contact GP if flare lasts >7 days, fever present, or a single
   hot/red/swollen joint (rule out septic arthritis — 999/A&E).

================================================================
6. UK BENEFITS — KEY FACTS
================================================================

- PIP (Personal Independence Payment): non-means-tested, up to
  £184.30/week (2024/25). Available 16 to State Pension age.
- Attendance Allowance: State Pension age and over, up to
  £108.55/week.
- Universal Credit: includes Limited Capability for Work element
  for those unable to work due to arthritis.
- Blue Badge: available if walking is significantly impaired.
- Motability scheme: lease a car using PIP enhanced mobility.
- Scotland: Adult Disability Payment replaces PIP.
- Around 70% of PIP appeals succeed at tribunal (Ministry of
  Justice, 2024).

================================================================
7. WHEN TO SEEK URGENT CARE
================================================================

- New severe headache, jaw pain or vision change in someone with
  PMR or over 50: possible giant cell arteritis — call 111/GP
  same day.
- Single hot, red, swollen joint with fever: possible septic
  arthritis — A&E.
- Sudden numbness, bladder/bowel changes with back pain:
  possible cauda equina — 999.
- Chest pain, breathlessness on a DMARD or biologic: contact
  rheumatology team urgently.

This site does not provide emergency medical advice. For urgent
symptoms, contact a GP, NHS 111 or 999.
